pr.title: Answer an agent's questions from Projector's band
pr.head: fc04c04a732e218bbfafa06459c7c561cfcb7f5b

summary: When a review or fix loop's subagent needs a decision from you, it can only hand the question to the main loop, which asks it as a line in the transcript. That line scrolls away, and your answer has no route back to the subagent. The questions plan fixes this in two pull requests. The first, #271, now merged into main, added project question, a command any host can run to ask, list, answer, and deliver questions. This second one builds Claude Code's view on top of that command, in Projector's band, the strip above the prompt that lists the pull requests your loops track.
The change gives Claude Code three things:

1. An ask tool. The model sees it as mcp__projector__ask from the first turn. The hooks module serves it by running project question ask, so a question asked through the tool and one asked from the shell land in the same store. The tool returns the question's reference, such as #337.3, at once, and the agent keeps working.
  2. Questions in the band. The questions are a bulleted list below the pull requests, oldest first, each line ending with its pull request and its age. Pressing a question opens a drawer that takes the band to itself: the detail, the numbered options with the recommendation first, a field for a typed answer, and discuss and dismiss.
  3. Answers through your prompt. Choosing an option records nothing. It puts the quoted question, a blank line, and the answer into your prompt. Sending that prompt answers the question: the band reads the answer back out of the sent text, records it, and marks it delivered, because the prompt carried it to the main loop. An answer given from a terminal is still claimed and delivered by the band, straight to a live subagent or to the main loop as a prompt of its own.
The plan stays in-progress. One acceptance row, opening a question's drawer on the main screen with ctrl+x tab and Enter, is a check by hand under tmux that has not been done.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• The store: project question's files for one session, one JSON file per question under $XDG_STATE_HOME/projector/questions/<session>/.
  • Reference: a question's fixed name, #337.3, owner/repo#337.3, or q2; an answer adds its letter, as #337.3.a.
  • Claim: a random token a deliverer takes on a recorded answer, so only one deliverer sends it. A claim lapses after a minute without renewal.
  • Route: send, a message to a live subagent through $.session.send, or submit, a prompt for the main loop through $.prompt.submit, which waits until the session is idle.
  • Signature: a string built from the store directory's file names, sizes and times, which the band compares on each tick to decide whether to read the store again.
  • Proposal: the text an option puts in the prompt, "<question>", a blank line, and the answer. The band finds answers in a sent prompt by looking for a quoted question that ends its line.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, at f1229f3, found that a failed store read was never retried. 51e8c80 fixed it.
  • The review of 382fb7f, which made your prompt carry the answer, found two problems. A quote answered every open question with the same text, and a prompt you did not send could answer a question. 6af99d9 and fc04c04 fix both: each quote answers one question, and only a composer or bridge prompt answers.
  • The review of fc04c04 opened one P2. The band remembers every drawer that filled the prompt until that question is answered, so a proposal you cleared still outranks the one you sent when two questions share their text. A flag marks it.
  • The gate passed at this head, including 50 hook tests under claude plugin test.

groups.title: The state and the pure helpers
groups.kicker: The types the band keeps and the logic that needs no engine
intro: Two files hold everything that can be tested without the engine. hooks/types.d.ts declares a Question as project question list --json prints it, and the two pieces of session state the band adds: bandQuestions, the band's last read of the store, and bandSending, each delivery in flight.

hooks/questions.ts holds the decisions: which text might hold a reference, the proposal an option puts in the prompt and how a sent prompt's answers are read back out (answersIn), the note that tells the main loop which subagent asked, whether an answer still needs a deliverer, which route it takes, where the store lives, the directory signature, and the ask tool's description, schema, and arguments.

checks.text: Session state survives a hot reload of the hooks module, while module variables do not. That is why each delivery's token, route, and text live in bandSending: a reloaded module can keep renewing a submit an earlier copy made, and recognize its prompt when it arrives.

files.note: Adds Question, Answer, and Sending, and the bandQuestions and bandSending state keys.

checks.text: bandSending is keyed by reference alone. That holds because the band only delivers questions from its own session's store.

files.note: The engine-free helpers: reference detection, proposals and reading answers back from a prompt, the relay note, delivery need, routing, the store path and signature, and the tool's schema and argument vector.

checks.text: These statuses match the engine's AgentStatus in the 2.1.296 plugin-authoring declarations, which lists completed, failed, and killed as the ended states.
A file whose claim the band itself renews counts by name alone, so the band's renewal every 5 seconds does not make it run project question list again.
I ran the vector this builds against the CLI in a temporary state directory: a question and a recommendation that start with - stay text, and a --detail value keeps its line break.

A quote goes first to the question earliest in proposed, and only an answer removes a ref from that list. When two open questions share their text and you fill the prompt from one drawer, clear it, then fill and send from the other, the first question takes the answer and its subagent is named in the relay note. Reproduced with #8.1 then #7.1, both asking Decline the finding?. Matching the proposed answer text, then the newest proposal, would route it right.

groups.title: The tool, the store read, answering, and delivery
groups.kicker: How the hooks module asks, reads, records, and delivers
intro: hooks/register.tsx wires the helpers into the engine. At session.start it registers the ask tool with isDeferred: false. Its tool.call hook runs project question ask and answers with the reference, or refuses with { deny }: the failed check for exit 65, the error and run project upgrade for another exit, and advice to ask in the conversation when project did not finish.

Every 5-second tick, shown or hidden, the band lists the store's directory and runs project question list only when the signature changed since the last successful read. A question it has not shown before shows the band.
An answer reaches the store one of two ways:

1. From your prompt. A drawer option fills the prompt with the quoted question and the answer. When you send the prompt, the prompt.submit hook finds each open question quoted at the end of a line, takes the next non-blank line as its answer, and adds a relay note to the prompt's context when a subagent asked. Once the prompt has entered, the band runs answer, claim, and delivered.
  2. From a terminal, or a dismissal. The band claims the recorded answer and sends it: through $.session.send to a live subagent, or otherwise through $.prompt.submit to the main loop, renewing the claim while that prompt waits. A dropped submit reopens the question.

The band's own submits are settled by the same prompt.submit hook when they arrive, so a hot reload never sends a second copy. The rest of the file draws the list and the drawer, which takes the band to itself while it is open.

checks.text: I checked each engine call against the 2.1.296 plugin-authoring declarations: $.tool.register with isDeferred, the tool.call answer as { result } or { deny }, SessionSendResult.isDelivered, PromptSubmitResult.drop, $.fs.list's entries, and a mobile surface without Input.

files.note: Registers and serves ask, reads the store on every tick, reads answers out of sent prompts, dismisses, claims and delivers terminal answers, attaches typed references, and draws the list and the drawer.

checks.text: The signature is recorded only after a read succeeds, so a failed read runs again on the next tick; the band test "a store read that fails runs again on the next tick" covers it.
proposed lives in the module, so a hot reload forgets it and a quote then goes to the oldest open question with that text.
Settling takes the entry out of bandSending in one state update before it runs the CLI, so the submit's own result and the prompt.submit hook settle a delivery once between them.
The reference joins delivering before the first await, so a tick cannot deliver this answer again while answer, claim, and delivered run.

Only a composer or bridge prompt is read for answers. A peer-send-message prompt that quotes an open question on its own line, run as a band test at this head, records nothing and leaves the question open.

Options are Markdown links, so a plain click fills the prompt and a ctrl, alt, or cmd click opens the pull request, or the question's file in the store when it has none. On the main screen a link takes no press, so an option there is answered through the typed field.
The whole question line is one plain Button with no hotkey, so a press anywhere opens the drawer and a digit typed first in an empty prompt presses nothing.
